title: Claude Agent Skills
hook: Agent Skills package instructions, scripts, and resources into folders an agent loads on demand — composable, portable expertise, later opened as a standard like MCP.
key_points: Anthropic feature (launched October 2025) for teaching Claude repeatable, specialized workflows.
A skill is a folder of instructions, scripts, and resources the agent discovers and loads when relevant.
Loaded on demand, so skills add capability without bloating the context window.
Released as an open standard in December 2025, echoing how MCP became an industry norm.
content_html: Agent Skills, introduced by Anthropic in October 2025, are a way to give an agent reusable, specialized expertise. A skill is simply a folder containing instructions, optional scripts, and supporting resources; the agent discovers available skills and loads the relevant one only when a task calls for it, rather than carrying all that knowledge in its prompt at all times.
extra_html:
What's new

The design's key move is loading on demand. Instead of stuffing every possible instruction into the context window, an agent reads a short description of each skill and pulls in the full contents only when needed — keeping the working context lean while making a large library of capabilities available. Anthropic shipped built-in skills (for documents like PPTX, XLSX, DOCX, PDF) plus support for custom skills across Claude.ai, Claude Code, and the API, and in December 2025 published the Skills format as an open standard.

Why it matters

Skills are a clean abstraction for the perennial problem of giving agents domain knowledge without overwhelming them. Making the format an open standard — the same playbook that turned the Model Context Protocol into a de facto norm for tool use — is a bid to define how the industry packages and shares agent capabilities, not just how one vendor does it.

related.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP): A Standard for Connecting LLMs to Tools
related.hook: MCP is an open protocol that standardizes how AI applications expose tools, data, and resources to models - think USB-C for AI tool integrations.

related.title: Claude Opus 4.7: Frontier Coding (2026)
related.hook: Claude Opus 4.7's gains land hardest on the hardest software-engineering tasks, and it now checks its own work - better self-verification of its outputs alongside the coding boost.

related.title: RESOURCE2SKILL: Distilling Executable Agent Skills from Human-Created Multimodal Resources
related.hook: Most agent skill libraries are hand-written text. This framework mines skills straight out of the tutorial videos, repos, and articles humans already made for each other.

related.title: The Regression Tax on Agent Skills
related.hook: Handing an agent a procedural skill doesn't only add wins — it also breaks tasks it used to solve. The best skills win by regressing less, not by gaining more.
